items.title: Marty Sheller interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 9, 2022
items.q: that was with Jackie McLean on alto and Bill Hardman on trumpet

ctx.x: Do you recall, let’s say you’re 12, 13, 14. What music made a lasting impression with you?

It began with the West Coast players, a group of friends that I had that we used to get together and play, we were listening to the guys out of the West Coast: Shorty Rogers and Stan Kenton, those kind of people. And I’ve thought about that and I realize that the reason probably was it was easier to understand. And matter of fact, when I went to high school one of the fellas in my high school was a very good tenor saxophone player and he laid a Miles Davis record on me and it was “Blue ’N’ Boogie,” one of those…
Terrific story. I remember that Café Bohemia is mentioned in Cannonball Adderley’s entrance into the jazz world also.
